newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ATLETICO AND AJAX BANKING ON SUCCESS IN EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLETICO AND AJAX BANKING ON SUCCESS IN EUROPE.

text.p: Atletico Madrid and Ajax know they have little else in the season left to play for as they prepare for Wednesday's eagerly-awaited European Cup quarter-final second leg tie.
After a 1-1 draw in Amsterdam in the first leg, the tie could hardly be more open.
The game is particularly vital for Antic's side, who may find themselves struggling to assure a place even in next season's UEFA Cup.
"It's our game of the year," coach Radomir Antic said.

Last year's Spanish double winners have seen their hopes of retaining their league and cup titles disappear in less than two weeks with three straight defeats in which they have conceded 12 goals in thrilling matches.
"Few times in my career I've lost three consecutive games playing so well," Antic said.
If Atletico were looking for peace and quiet ahead of the club's most important game of the year they could not have had a worse fortnight.
A last-minute goal at Real Betis led to defeat ten days ago while incidents during and after the match cost them suspensions to three key players.
Outspoken club president Jesus Gil replied by threatening to boycott the Spanish Cup.
In the event, Gil's players took a last minute plane to Barcelona for their cup tie and cruised into a 3-0 lead before going down 5-4.
Then last weekend they crashed 4-1 at home to Valencia.
Despite the setbacks Antic is optimistic.
"The motivation is great," he said. "We are not in a crisis situation and we are sufficiently good to knock out the Dutch."
Antic will wait to see whether striker Juan Eduardo Esnaider recovers from tonsilitis before chosing his team.
Esnaider's replacement could be fellow Argentine Leonardo Biagini, although Jose Luis Caminero could also be moved forward to partner Kiko Narvaez.
Patrick Kluivert's suspension is Ajax's biggest headache. The young Dutch striker had an uninspired game in Amsterdam but will be sorely missed by the Dutch champions, who must score in Madrid.
Ajax managed a satisfactory 3-1 home win over Roda JC on Friday thanks to the sparkling form of wingers Marc Overmars and Tijani Babangida. Both scored first half goals.
Finnish forward Jari Litmanen is still nursing a hip injury but hopes to be fit. Without Kluivert, Litmanen's presence will be essential.
Skipper Danny Blind and Ronald de Boer picked up minor injuries at the weekend but coach Luis van Gaal said he expected them to play.
Teams (probable):
Atletico Madrid - Jose Molina, Santi Denia, Toni Munoz, Roberto Solozabal, Juan Lopez, Radek Bejbl, Milinko Pantic, Diego Simeone, Jose Luis Caminero, Kiko Narvaez, Juan Eduardo Esnaider.
Ajax Amsterdam - Edwin van der Sar, Mario Melchiot, Danny Blind, Frank de Boer, Kiki Musampa, Arnold Scholten, Jari Litmanen, Richard Witschge, Tijani Babangida, Ronald de Boer, Marc Overmars.
